questions.q: What value is normally used as the null pointer at the end of a linked list?
questions.ok: Correct: the last node's pointer is -1.
questions.fb: The end of the list is marked by a null pointer, which the course uses as -1. Revisit section 01 (The idea).

questions.ok: Correct: it points at the first free slot.
questions.fb: heapStartPointer holds the index of the first free (unused) slot, because the unused positions are themselves kept as a linked list. See section 02 (Anatomy).
questions.model: The index of the first free (unused) position in the arrays.

questions.q: In the array implementation, how many arrays hold the list?
questions.ok: Correct: one array for data, one for pointers.
questions.fb: Exam questions use two parallel 1D arrays of the same size: one for data, one for the next-pointers. They do not use real memory addresses. See section 02.

questions.q: Using the arrays shown, what is the third item in the list order? (follow the pointers from startPointer)
questions.fb: Start at index 4 (16), its pointer is 1 so go to index 1 (19), whose pointer is 0, so index 0 (27). The third item is 27. Practise the trace tables in section 03.

questions.q: Using the same arrays, at which array index is the item 36 stored?
questions.fb: The data array is [27, 19, 36, 42, 16], so 36 is at index 2. The index where an item is stored is not its position in the list order.

questions.q: The find function starts its search at which index?
questions.fb: You do not scan from index 0. Start at startPointer and follow the chain of pointers. See section 03.
questions.code:
FUNCTION find(itemSearch) RETURNS INTEGER
  itemPointer <- startPointer
  found <- FALSE
  WHILE (itemPointer <> -1) AND NOT found DO
    IF myLinkedList[itemPointer] = itemSearch THEN
      found <- TRUE
    ELSE
      itemPointer <- myLinkedListPointers[itemPointer]
    ENDIF
  ENDWHILE
  RETURN itemPointer
ENDFUNCTION

questions.q: Look at the code. What value does the function return (the value left in itemPointer) when the item is not in the list?
questions.fb: The search failing is the outcome, but the function returns a value: when the loop ends without finding the item, itemPointer has followed the chain to the null pointer, -1. The code that called find treats -1 as 'not found'. Trace the loop in section 03.
questions.model: -1, the null pointer. The calling code reads -1 as 'not found'.
questions.code:
FUNCTION find(itemSearch) RETURNS INTEGER

  found <- FALSE

      found <- TRUE

    ENDIF
  ENDWHILE
  RETURN itemPointer

questions.q: When inserting a new node into the middle of a sorted linked list, which of these is NOT needed?
opts: Moving existing data items along the array
Taking a free slot from the heap
Giving the new node a pointer to the next node
questions.fb: The point of a linked list is that no data moves. You take a free slot, set the new node's pointer and redirect the previous node's pointer. See section 04.
questions.model: Moving existing data items along the array

questions.q: Explain one advantage of a linked list over a sorted array when inserting an item. (2 marks: state the advantage, then say why)
questions.ok: Full marks: you stated the advantage and explained why.
questions.fb: Two things are needed: the advantage (insertion is quicker or more efficient) and the reason (existing items do not have to be shifted along; only pointers are changed). See section 06.
questions.model: Insertion may be quicker, because items do not have to be shifted along to make room: only a couple of pointers need to change, so the amount of work is likely to stay small even for a long list.
questions.hint: State the advantage, then explain why it happens.
questions.fb_part: You have named a benefit (such as faster or quicker), which is the right idea, but the second mark needs the reason. In a sorted array every later item has to be shifted along to make room; in a linked list no data moves and only a couple of pointers are changed. Say why, not just that it is quicker. See section 06.

questions.q: A linked list is made from arrays of 12 elements and currently holds 5 items. How many nodes are on the heap?
questions.fb: Every position not in the list is on the heap (the free list). 12 − 5 = 7. See section 02.
